body.purpose: 14px system-UI work text; dense tables, forms, cards.

mono.purpose: Default mono stack; commands, diffs, SQL, backup codes. Four self-hosted coding faces (JetBrains Mono Nerd Mono, Fira Code, Cascadia Code, Source Code Pro) load only when a preference selects them.

shadows.name: floating-chrome

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Brand-teal fill, dark navy text, 6px radius — the only saturated action.

components.css: .ds-icon-btn { border: none; background: transparent; color: var(--ds-text-muted, #94A3B8); border-radius: var(--tblr-border-radius, 6px); padding: 0 .5rem; min-width: 44px; min-height: 44px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color .15s ease, color .15s ease; } .ds-icon-btn:hover, .ds-icon-btn:focus-visible { background: var(--tblr-bg-surface-secondary, #2A3B54); color: var(--ds-text, #FFFFFF); } .ds-icon-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ds-secondary, #00C2FF); outline-offset: -2px; } .ds-icon-btn:disabled { opacity: .45; cursor: not-allowed; background: transparent; } .ds-icon-danger { color: var(--ds-danger, #EF4444); } .ds-icon-danger:hover, .ds-icon-danger:focus-visible { color: var(--ds-danger, #EF4444); }

components.name: Ghost Key Button
components.description: Borderless text button for terminal key sends (Ctrl+C, Tab, Esc) — labels a glyph cannot carry.
components.css: .ds-ghost-btn { border: none; background: transparent; color: var(--ds-text-muted, #94A3B8); padding: 0 .75rem; min-height: 44px; border-radius: var(--tblr-border-radius, 6px); cursor: pointer; font-size: .875rem; transition: background-color .15s ease, color .15s ease; } .ds-ghost-btn:hover, .ds-ghost-btn:focus-visible { color: var(--ds-text, #FFFFFF); background: var(--tblr-bg-surface-secondary, #2A3B54); } .ds-ghost-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ds-secondary, #00C2FF); outline-offset: -2px; }

components.name: Status Lamp Badge
components.description: Low-tint status lamp (Tabler bg-*-lt family): state announced by tint plus text, never color alone.

components.description: File-folder silhouette of a terminal session tab: top-rounded, bottom border dropped, flush on the toolbar.

components.description: Surface-toned field, seam border, 6px radius; native focus ring.

narrative.overview: Precise, dense, quietly luminous. A dark operations deck that stays neutral until a signal needs your eye — then one lamp lights. The user is a developer operating their own machines; the interface is the instrument panel between them and every runtime, terminal, and database they own. It earns trust by being readable at a glance from across the room: deep navy surfaces, high-contrast instrument text, and a strict lamp discipline where teal means "act here," cyan means "go there," and status colors only ever announce states. Density is a feature, not a compromise. Tables are dense, chrome is compact, and workspace content — above all the terminal canvas — takes the majority of available space. Decoration has no lane: no decorative charts, no marketing gradients across page backgrounds, no chrome that competes with the PTY. Aesthetics come from discipline: 14px system type, 6px radii, borderless icon actions, and lamp badges doing all the emotional work. The dark theme is the default instrument (the app boots dark); light theme exists and flips surface/text tokens only, preserving the brand lamps. Light theme is a convenience for daylight, not a second identity.
keyCharacteristics: Dark navy workstation surfaces (Void Navy #0B1220 on Console Slate #1E293B), 14px system UI type, 6px corners.
One strict accent pair: Signal Teal #00E5A8 for primary actions/active states, Arc Cyan #00C2FF for links and navigation.
Status is lamps: low-tint Tabler badges (bg-*-lt) always paired with text or an icon, never color alone.
Borderless icon actions with 44×44px effective targets and inset focus rings; primary CTAs keep text labels.
Terminal-first: a pure-black xterm.js canvas with 60vh (70vh desktop) of workspace height; the gradient never approaches it.
Brand gradient (#00E5A8 → #00CFEA → #00C2FF) appears only in the logo lockup and restrained brand accents.

rules.name: The Gradient Lock Rule
rules.body: The teal→cyan brand gradient belongs to the logo lockup and restrained brand accents only. Never as a page background, a card fill, or anything near terminal output.

rules.name: The Lamp Rule
rules.body: Status never depends on color alone: every state pairs its lamp color with text or an icon, in a low-tint badge — not a saturated fill.

rules.name: The Neutral Glass Rule
rules.body: Terminal output is visually neutral. Brand colors and the gradient never tint terminal text; the terminal is real instruments, not marketing surface.

rules.name: The System Stack Rule
rules.body: No UI webfont is shipped. The interface renders in the platform's system stack — self-hosted means self-efficient; identity lives in the lamps, not letterforms.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Panels, cards, and tables sit flat on their surface. If an element is flat at rest, it gets depth from a tone step or a border, not a shadow.

dos: Do theme through the --ds-*/--bs-* tokens in app.css — new components inherit light/dark for free.
Do render small/secondary actions as .icon-btn (or .ghost-btn for key labels) with aria-label + title.
Do express state with a low-tint badge plus text/icon, and keep every component's loading/empty/error/disabled state real.
Do keep 44×44px effective targets and visible inset focus rings on chrome-less controls.
Do hide unimplemented sidebar sections entirely — never ship disabled placeholders.
Do use SweetAlert2 helpers for every dialog and Tabler patterns for every list state.
donts: Don't repaint primary actions white-on-teal, hand-roll button colors, or paint Tabler's default blue over the brand teal.
Don't use the brand gradient on page backgrounds, cards, or anywhere near terminal output.
Don't ship decorative charts or cards that don't help development work.
Don't use native window.alert/confirm/prompt or load a second Bootstrap copy alongside Tabler's.
Don't make essential behavior hover-only, color-only, or desktop-only.
Don't log or display credentials, tokens, terminal input/output, or file contents.
